items.followUp: Resolve a 100 N force acting at 30° to the horizontal into horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Defines resolution as replacing a force by its components.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that a force is split or resolved into components; award 1 mark if the answer only mentions components without explaining the process.

rubric.why: Identifies the usual perpendicular directions of the components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying perpendicular directions, such as horizontal and vertical.

rubric.why: Explains that the components together have the effect of the original force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the vector sum or resultant of the components equals the original force.

modelAnswer: Resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into two or more component forces.
The components are usually taken along perpendicular directions, such as the horizontal and vertical directions.
The vector sum (resultant) of the components is equal to the original force.
For a force F at angle θ to the horizontal, its components are Fₓ = F cos θ and Fᵧ = F sin θ.

items.followUp: A 120 N force acts on a 15 kg body from rest and gives it a speed of 40 m s⁻¹. Find the distance travelled while the force acts.

rubric.why: Identifies the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the force, mass, initial velocity and final velocity.

rubric.why: Uses Newton’s second law to find the acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using a = F/m and obtaining 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Selects the equation of motion that relates speed, acceleration and distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the correct equation.

rubric.why: Substitutes the values with appropriate units and solves for distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution and calculation leading to s = 125 m.

rubric.why: Gives the distance with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the answer 125 m.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, m = 20 kg, u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 50 m s⁻¹.
Using Newton’s second law: a = F/m = 200 N / 20 kg = 10 m s⁻².
Using v² = u² + 2as: (50 m s⁻¹)² = (0 m s⁻¹)² + 2(10 m s⁻²)s.
Distance = 125 m.

items.followUp: The density of a liquid is 800 kg m⁻³. Find the mass of 0.25 m³ of the liquid.

rubric.why: Finds the room’s volume from its dimensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for calculating V = 8 × 5 × 4 = 160 m³.

rubric.why: Uses the relationship between mass, density and volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating m = ρV.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given density and calculated volume and obtains the mass.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correct substitution and calculation; award 1 mark for correct substitution with an arithmetic error.

rubric.why: States the mass with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 208 kg.

modelAnswer: Given: ρ = 1.3 kg m⁻³; room dimensions = 8 m × 5 m × 4 m.
Volume of room: V = 8 m × 5 m × 4 m = 160 m³.
Formula: m = ρV.
Substitution: m = 1.3 kg m⁻³ × 160 m³ = 208 kg.
Mass of air in the room = 208 kg.

items.followUp: Define physics and name the branch that studies heat and its relationship with other forms of energy.

rubric.why: Includes the central subject matter of physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining physics as the study of matter, energy and their interaction or relationship.

rubric.why: Identifies the subject matter of mechanics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mechanics deals with the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.

modelAnswer: Physics is the branch of science that deals with matter, energy and their interaction or relationship.
Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring instrument? State the usual least count of a micrometer screw gauge.

rubric.why: Defines least count as the smallest measurement an instrument can measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition referring to the smallest measurable value or division.

rubric.why: States the standard least count of Vernier callipers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0.1 mm or its equivalent, 0.01 cm.

modelAnswer: Least count is the smallest measurement that can be measured accurately by an instrument.
The usual least count of Vernier callipers is 0.1 mm (0.01 cm).

items.followUp: Define plasma and geophysics, and state the main subject studied in each.

rubric.why: Identifies plasma as an ionized gas containing charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining plasma as an ionized gas or mentioning its ions and free electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies geophysics as the application of physics to the study of Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking geophysics with the study of Earth and its physical properties using physics.

modelAnswer: Plasma is an ionized gas containing free electrons and positive ions; it is a state of matter.
Geophysics is the branch of physics that applies physical principles to study the Earth and its physical properties.

items.followUp: Define rotational motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Describes the shared motion of points in a body undergoing translation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all points of a body move the same distance in the same direction in the same time interval.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of translatory motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as a car moving along a straight road.

modelAnswer: Translatory motion is motion in which all points of a body move the same distance in the same direction in the same time interval.
Example: a car moving along a straight road.

items.followUp: Why are roads banked at curves?

rubric.why: Describes how a road is banked at a curve.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the outer edge of a curved road is raised above the inner edge.

rubric.why: Explains the purpose of banking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that banking helps provide centripetal force or helps prevent skidding while turning.

modelAnswer: Banking of roads is the raising of the outer edge of a curved road above its inner edge.
It helps provide the required centripetal force and reduces the chance of vehicles skidding while turning.
